thesis:
— why this matters to the AI sector

The strongest reading of the Koa announcement is that it is the first time a large enterprise software vendor has publicly converted "we were renting intelligence" from a cost complaint into a product strategy — and the numbers on both sides of that trade make it concrete. Salesforce's own AI engineering chief, Jayesh Govindarajan, wrote in July 2026 that eighteen months earlier "Agentforce also ran entirely on a single rented model, and our token bill grew linearly with traffic," and that rather than pass the bill on to customers, Salesforce "opted to rebuild" by tuning targeted open-source models for individual jobs; he describes the resulting inference architecture in the language of *architectural agency* — the ability to "swap the foundation models freely, instead of being dependent on any single vendor" — and reports that a purpose-built classifier answers in ~50 milliseconds where a general model takes roughly a second (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/cutting-inference-spend-by-right-sizing-models/). Koa is that logic pushed one layer up the stack: instead of renting frontier reasoning from Anthropic or OpenAI through Agentforce's AI gateway, Salesforce post-trained NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3 Super on a synthetic corpus derived from 27 years of its own CRM deployments, claims it matches or beats leading general models on CRM actions "with three times fewer errors," and asserts that it is cheaper in tokens than sending the same tasks to Claude or ChatGPT — while keeping the weights and the inference inside its own trust boundary (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/; https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear). The strategic significance is not that a CRM model got better at routing cases; it is that the scarce asset in enterprise AI has quietly shifted from *model capability* to *proprietary process telemetry* — Salesforce's argument is explicitly that "the most valuable thing Salesforce has built isn't our platform — it's the accumulated knowledge of how enterprise business actually works," which is precisely the input the frontier labs do not have and cannot buy. That framing lands on top of a market where Gartner now projects **$2.59 trillion in worldwide AI spending in 2026, up 47% Y/Y**, with AI-model spending growth revised up to **110%** for the year (https://www.01net.it/gartner-forecasts-worldwide-ai-spending-to-grow-47-in-2026) — while simultaneously warning that up to **$234 billion of enterprise application spending is exposed to "agentic arbitrage" by 2030**, because "agentic systems deliver outcomes directly… making the software invisible" and thereby "break[ing] the link between user growth and revenue growth" (https://businessnewsthisweek.com/business/gartner-says-dollar-234-billion-in-enterprise-application-software-spend-is-at-risk-from-agentic-ai). Koa is an incumbent's answer to both halves of that squeeze: defend the software layer by owning the reasoning that acts on it, and defend the margin by no longer paying frontier prices for work that a domain-specific model can do better and cheaper. The two caveats that keep this honest: **Koa is pilot-only with GA "expected winter 2026 in U.S. regions," and its headline benchmark is a Salesforce-authored internal benchmark with no published methodology, no error-rate baseline, and no independent reproduction** — so the real test is not today's benchmark slide but whether the token-cost advantage survives contact with customer workloads at GA, and whether Salesforce's insistence on routing around frontier providers holds when it continues to simultaneously ship Anthropic's Claudeforce and offer rival models through Amazon Bedrock (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/aws-salesforce-enterprise-ai-expansion/). If Koa's economics hold, the read-through for the AI sector is a durable ceiling on frontier-lab enterprise pricing power and a rising premium on *proprietary workflow data* as the moat — with Salesforce's $1.5B+ Agentforce ARR, up over 240% Y/Y (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108524/000110852426000187/crm-q2fy27xexhibit991.htm), as the first scaled evidence that enterprises will pay for that trade.

# The Signal — Research Fact Sheet

**Story:** Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) and NVIDIA unveil **Koa**, Salesforce's first CRM reasoning model, built on NVIDIA Nemotron, for the Agentforce platform — announced at Dreamforce 2026.
**Article date:** Tuesday, September 15, 2026
**Ticker:** CRM | **Sector slug:** `ai`
**FINAL SLUG:** `salesforce-koa-reasoning-model-agentforce-2026` (confirmed as supplied by orchestrator — unique, do not alter)
**Analyst:** Nelly | **Sources:** primary-first; every bullet carries its URL. Figures marked UNVERIFIED where no primary/syndicated source could be confirmed.
**Fact count:** 59 numbered, URL-bearing facts — deliberately above the 25–40 range requested, because several bullets bundle multi-part primary-source claims (e.g. full quarterly guidance mechanics, Nemotron 3 Super specs). Nothing here is padding; trim at the article stage, not the research stage. `verified_facts_count` = 59.

---

## 1. The announcement itself (primary source)

1. Salesforce and NVIDIA announced **Koa on September 15, 2026** — Salesforce's first CRM reasoning model, built on NVIDIA Nemotron, for Agentforce. Dateline: "SAN FRANCISCO, September 15, 2026." — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
2. Salesforce article subhead: **"Koa is trained with 27 years of Salesforce CRM intelligence to enable agents to reason through the complex, multistep tasks required for enterprise work."** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
3. **"Koa was built by post-training NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super with a proprietary synthetic dataset modeled on enterprise knowledge from nearly three decades of CRM deployments."** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
4. Verbatim benchmark claim: **"In Salesforce's CRM benchmark, a model benchmark that includes a suite of real-world tasks like updating an opportunity, routing a case, or scheduling a follow-up, Koa already matches or exceeds leading model performance on CRM actions with three times fewer errors."** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
5. **"No customer data was used to train the Koa reasoning model."** Its training corpus was built entirely from synthetic scenarios reflecting the reasoning, tool use, and decision-making skills Agentforce agents perform across CRM workflows: **generating leads, qualifying opportunities, and resolving service cases across the customer lifecycle.** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
6. Synthetic scenarios were built to simulate real-world enterprise workflows **"across more than 14 industries, including manufacturing, financial services, healthcare, and travel."** Each scenario **"paired a persona with specific tasks then mapped the sequence of actions and tool calls an agent must take to complete them."** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
7. Training method: **"Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with NVIDIA NeMo RL, NeMo Gym, and NeMo AutoModel."** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
8. Control/boundary claim: **"Salesforce controls the weights and runs Koa within its own infrastructure, ensuring that no customer data crosses the trust boundary during inference."** Separately: **"Salesforce controls the model weights and performs post-training and inference entirely within its own trust boundary."** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
9. **Availability (verbatim):** "Koa: Available to select pilot customers now in Agentforce; **general availability expected winter 2026 in U.S. regions.**" It is **pilot-only today, NOT GA.** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
10. Koa is **already in internal production use at Salesforce**, including **"an agent in Slack that helps employees find information and complete everyday tasks in Slack."** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
11. Named customer pilots: **1-800Accountant, Baxter Credit Union (BCU), Engine, Formula 1, UChicago Medicine, and Xero** — "moving into customer pilots." — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
12. **Marc Benioff (Chair and CEO, Salesforce), verbatim:** "The most valuable thing Salesforce has built isn't our platform — it's the accumulated knowledge of how enterprise business actually works. With Koa, the knowledge is put inside the model itself. We trained a reasoning engine that understands the structure of a deal, the lifecycle of a service case, and the workflows that vary across industries. That's a different kind of intelligence, and it runs entirely inside your trust boundary." — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
13. **Jensen Huang (founder and CEO, NVIDIA), verbatim:** "AI is creating a much larger opportunity for software. Every company needs useful AI, tailored to its knowledge, expertise, and work. NVIDIA Nemotron open models give Salesforce the foundation to turn decades of enterprise expertise into specialized AI with Koa, creating a CRM model that can reason and securely take action." — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
14. **Ryan Teeples (Chief Strategy Officer, 1-800Accountant), verbatim:** "Accounting requires navigating tax rules, financial data, documents, and the unique circumstances of every customer. Koa gives our agents the reasoning to work through that complexity step by step and use the right tools along the way…" — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
15. **John Sahagian (SVP and Chief Data Officer, Baxter Credit Union), verbatim:** "Our members come to us with goals, whether that's buying a home, managing their money, or planning for what's next. Koa can help our Digital agents understand the full complexity and context behind those goals…" — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
16. **Elia Wallen (Founder and CEO, Engine), verbatim:** "Business travel has countless moving parts, and what we need from AI isn't a model that sounds confident — it's one that can reason precisely through complex, multi-step problems." — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
17. **A 6th named customer quote the orchestrator's brief omitted — Andrew Chang (Chief Marketing Officer, UChicago Medicine):** "Koa can work across those longer, multi-step workflows and help our teams manage that complexity more effectively. That creates more time and capacity for what matters most, caring for patients." — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
18. **Missionforce thread:** Salesforce and NVIDIA are "bringing Nemotron-based models and accelerated computing into Missionforce," extending control over model, data, and deployment environment to government/regulated orgs — for **"private clouds, air-gapped networks, and other secure environments."** — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/
19. Missionforce timeline (verbatim): "Missionforce Operations: **Product generally available now in U.S. regions. Post-trained NVIDIA models available to select customers in October 2026.**" — https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/

## 2. Secondary coverage — the quotes the orchestrator asked for

20. **Jayesh Govindarajan (EVP of Salesforce AI) — verbatim, the "previously relied on frontier providers" quote:** "We've built many small task-specific language models, which are part of Agentforce's portfolio. **But reasoning has always been something that we've relied on the frontier model providers for. Until now.**" (Interview with TechCrunch's Julie Bort, published 5:00 AM PDT, September 15, 2026.) — https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear
21. Govindarajan, second verbatim quote on why not before: "One of the reasons we hadn't done this before, train our own enterprise-grade frontier model — we always wanted to — but the challenge has always been the lack of a pre-trained base model to start with. **Until Nemotron came along, there was no sovereign American pre-trained model that was available, one, and two, that was state of the art, and, three, that had clear data provenance. We have no idea what Qwen trains on.**" — https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear
22. Govindarajan on the synthetic-data method, verbatim: "We actually simulated a customer service environment with a persona customer service professional, including irate customers that call into the customer service center, all the way to a sales professional who's trying to close a deal." — https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear
23. **Token-cost claim — verbatim:** "**Koa is meant to be better at the work tasks Salesforce customers want an agent to do — and cheaper, in terms of tokens burned — than sending those same tasks to Claude or ChatGPT.**" (TechCrunch states no specific percentage or price delta; **UNVERIFIED as to magnitude**.) — https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear
24. Routing context from TechCrunch: "Before Koa, if an agent needed to reason through a long-running or multi-step task, those prompts would be routed to a frontier model like Claude or ChatGPT through Agentforce's AI gateway (the system that decides which model handles which request)." — https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear
25. **Kari Ann Briski (NVIDIA VP of Generative AI Software for Enterprise), verbatim:** "It's kind of the trifecta of things that you need to have: sovereign AI, time to first token, efficient reasoning, for the tokenomics of it all." — https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear
26. **Rohan Kumar (Chief Platform and Engineering Officer, Salesforce) — no-customer-data quote:** Kumar **"insisted that it has not tapped any of the vast volumes of customer information stored within its CRM platform. Instead, the company used its customer data to build a massive synthetic dataset crafted out of almost 30 years' worth of internal CRM deployment experiences."** — https://siliconangle.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-debuts-koa-a-specialized-model-built-to-reason-over-crm-data
27. **Kumar, verbatim on genesis:** "There is so much knowledge that we've sort of gathered in building out the CRM over the last 27 years… And there is this talk around domain-specific models, which take the intelligence the model already has and you then post-train the model. Basically adding more information specific to a certain kind of job. **That's the genesis of Koa.**" — https://siliconangle.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-debuts-koa-a-specialized-model-built-to-reason-over-crm-data
28. SiliconANGLE independently reports the benchmark: Koa "matching or exceeding the performance of multiple leading general-purpose models on CRM-based tasks **with three times fewer errors**." Also confirms Koa is **"still isn't generally available yet… available to select customers via an expanded pilot program within the Agentforce platform. General availability is slated for winter, Kumar said."** — https://siliconangle.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-debuts-koa-a-specialized-model-built-to-reason-over-crm-data
29. TechCrunch's framing (useful for the thesis, but it is an opinionated characterization, not a Salesforce claim): Koa is "a shining example of how the enterprise world's needs for AI are diverging from what the frontier labs are offering," and lists an **"open-weight alternative to closed frontier models."** ⚠️ Caveat: Salesforce's own release says Salesforce **controls the weights** and runs inference in its own boundary — it does not describe Koa itself as open-weight. Do not repeat "open-weight Koa" as fact. — https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear
30. TechCrunch: Salesforce is **not abandoning Anthropic/OpenAI** — it "just announced a partnership with Anthropic called **Claudeforce**." — https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear

## 3. Dreamforce 2026

31. **Dreamforce 2026 dates and city (primary): "September 15–17, 2026 | San Francisco and Salesforce+"**, with a "Trailblazer Bootcamp at Dreamforce | Sept 12–14." Koa, AIforce, the AWS/Google Cloud expansions and the Siemens deepening were all announced at/for Dreamforce 2026. — https://www.salesforce.com/dreamforce/
32. Attendance: "**Dreamforce welcomes more than 43,000 to San Francisco** amid debate over pace of AI development" (ABC7 Bay Area, September 14, 2026). — https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=Dreamforce%202026%20dates%20San%20Francisco&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US:en (headline + source: ABC7 Bay Area, 2026-09-14 03:18 UTC; syndicated as "Dreamforce welcomes 43K+ to SF amid debate over pace of AI" — Yahoo)

33. **Nemotron 3 Super is the model Koa was post-trained from, first launched March 11, 2026 — verbatim spec (NVIDIA Blog, by Kari Briski):** "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super is a **120-billion-parameter open model with 12 billion active parameters**"; "**Nemotron 3 Super has a 1-million-token context window**"; a "**hybrid mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture**" combining Mamba layers (4x memory/compute efficiency) with transformer layers, **latent MoE** (four experts activated for the cost of one) and **multi-token prediction** (3x faster inference); "up to **5x higher throughput and up to 2x higher accuracy** than the previous Nemotron Super model"; runs in **NVFP4 on NVIDIA Blackwell**, "up to 4x faster than FP8 on NVIDIA Hopper, with no loss in accuracy"; released with **open weights under a permissive license**; "The model was trained on synthetic data." — https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nemotron-3-super-agentic-ai/
34. **The EARLIER, DIFFERENT announcement — do not conflate:** On **March 16, 2026** (GTC week, not Dreamforce), Salesforce and NVIDIA announced "Salesforce Teams With NVIDIA to Bring High-Performance, Cost-Efficient AI Agents Into the Flow of Enterprise Work," in which **"NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano is available within Agentforce"** with a **1 million token context window** and a **Mixture of Experts architecture**. Direct guesses against nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/<koa-slug> return the generic archive/200 shell, not an article. **Conclusion: the Koa announcement lives on the Salesforce properties; treat "NVIDIA also issued a Koa press release" as UNVERIFIED.** — https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news ; https://blogs.nvidia.com/feed/

## 9. THESIS — why this matters to the AI sector

The strongest reading of the Koa announcement is that it is the first time a large enterprise software vendor has publicly converted "we were renting intelligence" from a cost complaint into a product strategy — and the numbers on both sides of that trade make it concrete. Salesforce's own AI engineering chief, Jayesh Govindarajan, wrote in July 2026 that eighteen months earlier "Agentforce also ran entirely on a single rented model, and our token bill grew linearly with traffic," and that rather than pass the bill on to customers, Salesforce "opted to rebuild" by tuning targeted open-source models for individual jobs; he describes the resulting inference architecture in the language of *architectural agency* — the ability to "swap the foundation models freely, instead of being dependent on any single vendor" — and reports that a purpose-built classifier answers in ~50 milliseconds where a general model takes roughly a second (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/cutting-inference-spend-by-right-sizing-models/). Koa is that logic pushed one layer up the stack: instead of renting frontier reasoning from Anthropic or OpenAI through Agentforce's AI gateway, Salesforce post-trained NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3 Super on a synthetic corpus derived from 27 years of its own CRM deployments, claims it matches or beats leading general models on CRM actions "with three times fewer errors," and asserts that it is cheaper in tokens than sending the same tasks to Claude or ChatGPT — while keeping the weights and the inference inside its own trust boundary (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/koa-reasoning-model/; https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/salesforce-and-nvidias-new-reasoning-model-is-everything-the-ai-labs-should-fear). The strategic significance is not that a CRM model got better at routing cases; it is that the scarce asset in enterprise AI has quietly shifted from *model capability* to *proprietary process telemetry* — Salesforce's argument is explicitly that "the most valuable thing Salesforce has built isn't our platform — it's the accumulated knowledge of how enterprise business actually works," which is precisely the input the frontier labs do not have and cannot buy. That framing lands on top of a market where Gartner now projects **$2.59 trillion in worldwide AI spending in 2026, up 47% Y/Y**, with AI-model spending growth revised up to **110%** for the year (https://www.01net.it/gartner-forecasts-worldwide-ai-spending-to-grow-47-in-2026) — while simultaneously warning that up to **$234 billion of enterprise application spending is exposed to "agentic arbitrage" by 2030**, because "agentic systems deliver outcomes directly… making the software invisible" and thereby "break[ing] the link between user growth and revenue growth" (https://businessnewsthisweek.com/business/gartner-says-dollar-234-billion-in-enterprise-application-software-spend-is-at-risk-from-agentic-ai). Koa is an incumbent's answer to both halves of that squeeze: defend the software layer by owning the reasoning that acts on it, and defend the margin by no longer paying frontier prices for work that a domain-specific model can do better and cheaper. The two caveats that keep this honest: **Koa is pilot-only with GA "expected winter 2026 in U.S. regions," and its headline benchmark is a Salesforce-authored internal benchmark with no published methodology, no error-rate baseline, and no independent reproduction** — so the real test is not today's benchmark slide but whether the token-cost advantage survives contact with customer workloads at GA, and whether Salesforce's insistence on routing around frontier providers holds when it continues to simultaneously ship Anthropic's Claudeforce and offer rival models through Amazon Bedrock (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/aws-salesforce-enterprise-ai-expansion/). If Koa's economics hold, the read-through for the AI sector is a durable ceiling on frontier-lab enterprise pricing power and a rising premium on *proprietary workflow data* as the moat — with Salesforce's $1.5B+ Agentforce ARR, up over 240% Y/Y (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108524/000110852426000187/crm-q2fy27xexhibit991.htm), as the first scaled evidence that enterprises will pay for that trade.
